issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20223 - Add drag-and-drop reordering for schema form arrays
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds drag-and-drop reordering to array items in the ui-v2 schema form using @dnd-kit. Each reorderable item gets a GripVertical drag handle, prefix items (tuples) get a spacer instead, and the existing move up/down menu items are kept. The wiring is in `schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, which wraps the list in a `DndContext` and `SortableContext`, and in `schema-form-input-array-item.tsx`, which calls `useSortable` and renders the handle.

The drop handler has a real correctness bug. `handleDragEnd` calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem` takes `(from, to)`, so the arguments are reversed. Dragging the first item onto the third slot moves the third item to the top instead. Nothing in the drop path also stops a regular item from landing in a prefix-item slot. The tests are snapshot-only: they check DOM structure but none exercise dragging, the move up/down menu, or the prefix restriction, even though the PR description says they do. The snapshot tests could not catch the reversed-index bug.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The reversed `moveItem` arguments break the core feature: a drag reorders the wrong item. Prefix-item protection is only enforced on the drag source, not on the drop target. The PR description claims behavioral tests for move up/down and prefix immobility that are not in the diff, so the bug went unnoticed. These need fixing and a behavioral test before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `SchemaFormInputArrayList` rendered each array item as a `SchemaFormInputArrayItem` row. Reordering happened only through the per-item dropdown (Move up / Move down), which calls `moveItem(from, to)`. That function splices the local keyed-values state and then calls `onValuesChange`, which passes the new array up to the parent form.

This PR wraps the same list in a dnd-kit `DndContext` with pointer and keyboard sensors, and a `SortableContext` keyed by each item's stable uuid. Each row calls `useSortable` with `disabled: !canMove`, so prefix items are not draggable and show a spacer where the handle would be. The drag end handler maps the active and over keys to indices and reuses `moveItem`, so the menu and drag paths share one state mutation.
steps: Entry point: `SchemaFormInputArrayList` (schema-form-input-array-list.tsx) owns `localKeyedValues`, keyed by uuid, and is the only place that calls `onValuesChange`.
Drag wiring: the list now wraps its rows in `DndContext` (closestCenter, pointer and keyboard sensors) and `SortableContext` (verticalListSortingStrategy), and passes `itemKey` to each row.

Row behavior: `SchemaFormInputArrayItem` calls `useSortable`, applies the transform and opacity to its root div, and renders a GripVertical button as the drag handle when `canMove` is true, or a `w-5` spacer for prefix items.
Drop path: `handleDragEnd` resolves active and over keys to indices and calls `moveItem`. The diagram shows this path; the review notes flag its argument order and missing prefix guard.
Menu path (unchanged): the Move up and Move down dropdown items still call `moveItem(index, index ± 1)` directly, so both paths end in the same state update and `onValuesChange` call.
Tests: the snapshot file gains four `array` cases that pin DOM structure, including handles and prefix spacers. No tests cover dragging, menu reordering, or the prefix restriction.

findings.title: Drag-end passes indices to moveItem in reverse order
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (around lines 130-145) calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem(from, to)` is defined at lines 117-122 and takes the source index first. Swap the arguments so the dragged item's old index is `from` and its new index is `to`, matching how the Move up/down menu calls `moveItem(index, index - 1)`. Then add a behavioral test that drags item 0 to position 2 and asserts the resulting order, so this regression is covered.

findings.title: Regular items can be dropped onto prefix-item slots
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (about lines 130-145) must not let a drop land on a prefix-item index. `getCanMoveForIndex` (lines 93-98) already defines prefix membership as `index < property.prefixItems.length`. In `handleDragEnd`, after computing `oldIndex` and `newIndex`, return early if either index is a prefix index, or if the dragged item is a prefix item. Optionally, pass only the movable keys to `SortableContext` so prefix items are excluded from sorting. Add a test that a regular item dropped on a prefix slot leaves the prefix order unchanged.

findings.title: PR claims behavioral tests that the diff does not contain
findings.body:
The PR description lists "Behavioral tests for move up/down menu options" and a "Test verifying prefix items cannot be moved". The only test changes are four snapshot cases under `describe("array")` (lines 489-565). The `.snap` file shows DOM structure only. Nothing clicks a drag handle, opens the menu and selects Move up or Move down, or checks the value passed to `onValuesChange`. That is why the reversed `moveItem` arguments were not caught. The snapshots also pass whether or not the handle works. Behavioral tests are needed for the drag-end logic, the menu path, and the prefix restriction.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx" lines="489-565"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add behavioral tests to `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx` (or a new `schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx`) for the array reorder paths. Cover: (1) the Move up and Move down menu items reorder items and call `onValuesChange` with the correct array; (2) prefix items have no drag handle and no Move up or Move down entries; (3) a drag-end event moves the dragged item to the expected position, which can be triggered by simulating dnd-kit's `onDragEnd` or keyboard sort. Use the existing `TestSchemaForm` helper and assert on the values the form receives, not on mock call counts. Update the PR description if these tests are not added.

findings.title: Drag handle removes its focus ring, hurting keyboard use
findings.body:
The handle's class list includes `focus:outline-none`, and no replacement focus style is provided. The PR says keyboard reordering works by tabbing to the handle and using the arrow keys, and the `KeyboardSensor` is wired up for that. But a keyboard user gets no visible indication of which handle has focus. The rest of this codebase uses `focus-visible:ring-*` (for example the menu trigger in the snapshot), so the handle should follow the same pattern.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx" lines="83-95"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx`, the drag handle button (around lines 83-92) uses `focus:outline-none` with no replacement. Replace it with the focus-visible ring classes the other icon buttons in this form use (for example `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-ring`, as on the dropdown trigger in the snapshot). Then update the snapshot files for the array tests.

findings.title: prefixItemsCount is computed but never used
findings.body:
`prefixItemsCount` is declared at lines 45-47 and is not referenced anywhere in the file. The prefix check is done elsewhere with `isArray(property.prefixItems) && index < property.prefixItems.length`. Either use the variable in the drop guard (see the high-severity finding on prefix drops) or remove it.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="45-47"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, the `prefixItemsCount` constant at lines 45-47 is unused. If the prefix guard in `handleDragEnd` is added, use this value there, or reuse it in `getCanMoveForIndex` (lines 93-98). Otherwise delete it.

findings.title: Comment above sortableKeys says it filters, but the code does not
findings.body:
The comment at line 147 says "Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)", but line 148 maps over every item, prefix items included. The comment describes behavior the code does not have, and it hides the prefix-drop issue above. Either filter the keys as the comment says or correct the comment.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="147-148"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx` at lines 147-148, the comment says `sortableKeys` contains only non-prefix items, but `localKeyedValues.map(...)` includes all items. Decide which behavior is intended. If prefix items should stay out of sorting, filter with `getCanMoveForIndex` before mapping to keys. If not, rewrite the comment to match the code.

findings.title: Drag-and-drop uses dnd-kit with keyboard support and disabled-by-prefix handling
findings.body: The stable uuid keys are passed as `itemKey` and used as the `useSortable` ids, which avoids index-based identity during reorders. Prefix rows are disabled with `useSortable({ disabled: !canMove })` and show a spacer, so the handle is conditional rather than hidden with CSS. The `KeyboardSensor` with `sortableKeyboardCoordinates` gives keyboard reordering without custom code. The menu-based fallback is kept, and both paths share `moveItem`.
